findings.title: Null check for rawTokenId duplicates grantType check
findings.body: The constructor checks `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` but tests grantType again. rawTokenId is never null-checked, so a null rawTokenId is accepted and the intended validation is missing (the message also refers to the wrong variable).

findings.title: Token ID parsing assumes fixed 6-char prefix, length check throws on any unexpected input
findings.body: getTokenContextFromTokenId throws IllegalArgumentException for any token ID whose prefix before ':' is not exactly 6 characters or has unknown shortcuts. Callers reading tokens (introspection, userinfo, account REST) will fail hard on malformed or foreign IDs instead of degrading gracefully to UNKNOWN, which the no-colon branch already does. Inconsistent handling can turn a bad/legacy-format token into a 500 error.

findings.title: Null token ID causes NullPointerException
findings.body: getTokenContextFromTokenId calls encodedTokenId.indexOf without a null check; a null id (e.g. token without jti) causes an NPE rather than a clear result.

findings.title: Shortcut maps are populated in postInit but used in init-time-independent lookups; unsafe for lazily-discovered grants
findings.body: getGrantTypeByShortcut/getShortcutByGrantType mutate ConcurrentHashMaps from request threads and call sessionFactory.getProviderFactory on every miss. Unknown grant names or shortcuts trigger a full stream scan on every token request and a map write, causing repeated lookup cost and potentially unbounded map growth from attacker-influenced values only if grant names are influenced; the rebuild also isn't atomic with the two-map consistency check.

findings.title: ClassCastException risk when casting provider factories
findings.body: getShortcutByGrantType casts the result of getProviderFactory(OAuth2GrantType.class, ...) to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory without checking; any custom OAuth2GrantType factory not implementing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory would throw ClassCastException during token creation.

findings.title: Token ID encoding throws for grants without shortcut, breaking token creation
findings.body: initToken now calls encoder.encodeTokenId, which throws IllegalStateException when the grant type is unknown (the default when no GRANT_TYPE attribute is set, e.g. flows that never set Constants.GRANT_TYPE such as login/browser flows, token refresh paths or other callers of createClientAccessToken). Access token creation can therefore fail for legitimate flows instead of degrading to an 'na' grant.

findings.title: Encoding fails for grant types that are not in the factory map
findings.body: encodeTokenId throws when the grant type has no shortcut, so any grant type added without an OAuth2GrantTypeFactory shortcut (or a custom grant) breaks access token issuance rather than falling back to the UNKNOWN shortcut used elsewhere.

findings.title: Grant type attribute set from request params, not the actual grant
findings.body: createTokenResponse sets GRANT_TYPE from context.getGrantType(), which reads the raw form parameter grant_type. Token exchange and PreAuthorized paths set their own constant, so the stored value can disagree with the grant actually processed; the token ID shortcut then reflects client input rather than the server-side grant.

findings.title: Refresh grant type hard-coded in validateToken
findings.body: validateToken sets GRANT_TYPE to REFRESH_TOKEN for token recreation, but this path can be reached from non-refresh callers (e.g. introspection/userinfo validation), giving the recreated token an inaccurate grant shortcut in its ID.

findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher logic is inverted and fails to validate
findings.body: The matcher returns false when the grant shortcut equals the expected value (`if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`), i.e. it rejects exactly the correct token. Also the shortcut is at chars 4-5 (index 4..6 of the 6-char prefix), and substring(3,5) is off by one. Event assertions will fail or pass incorrectly.

findings.title: Incorrect-grant test catches any RuntimeException
findings.body: testIncorrectGrantType wraps the call in try/catch RuntimeException, so the test passes even when the Assert.fail fails path is hit inside... actually Assert.fail throws AssertionError (not caught), but any unrelated RuntimeException also passes the test. Should use assertThrows with IllegalArgumentException.

findings.title: Error message names wrong parameter
findings.body: The second requireNonNull on grantType uses the message 'Null rawTokenId not allowed', which is misleading; it is the rawTokenId that is not checked at all.
